title: Auth Observability After‑Action: RBACv2, SSO & Audit Pipeline SLOs/Alerts Remediation
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Summary: This ticket consolidates findings from the March 2026 auth/audit availability incident and defines a prioritized remediation plan across three areas: RBACv2 policy evaluation latency, SSO/SAML session handling under spike load, and the audit-event delivery pipeline. The goal is to make the auth surface observable and resilient with concrete SLOs and tuned alerting so regressions are caught earlier and with actionable signals.

What triggered this: A region-level capacity spike caused transient delays in token validation and SAML assertions leading to failed sign-ins and delayed audit-event ingestion. Multiple signals were noisy (high auth latency, partial 502s from the auth proxy, and audit sink lag), which slowed incident diagnosis.

High-level proposed outcomes: 1) Define and publish auth SLOs and error budgets; 2) Reduce blind spots by adding end-to-end observability for RBAC eval timing and SAML hops; 3) Rationalize and tune alerts to reduce paging for known low‑impact noise; 4) Implement prioritized fixes for audit pipeline delivery reliability.

SLO examples to adopt (targets are initial proposals to be iterated):
- Auth API latency: 99th percentile <= 200ms (token validation + RBAC eval)
- Auth API availability: 99.95% (errors resulting in user-facing failures)
- Audit event delivery: 99.5% delivered to primary sink within 30s
- SSO login end-to-end success rate: 99.9% over 24h window

Rationale: These targets align with platform SLAs and aim to prioritize user-visible failures first. Audit delivery SLO is slightly lower given queueing characteristics but must be observable so integrity concerns are caught quickly.
acceptance_criteria: SLOs documented and published in the security-observability playbook page
Dashboards created for RBAC evaluation latency (p50/p95/p99), SSO end-to-end flow duration, and audit sink lag
Alert rules updated to the new signal taxonomy with runbooks attached
Top 3 engineering fixes deployed and validated (see action items)
Post-rollout run (72h) shows reduced noisy pages and no regression in auth success rate
comments: 2026-03-06 - Ethan Park: Initial incident notes uploaded; linked raw traces and Kinesis audit lag metrics. See links for dumps.
2026-03-07 - Leah Morrison: Assigned and triaged. Prioritized observable gaps: RBAC eval timing not emitted, SAML duration only in ingress proxy, audit sink lacks delivery timestamps.
2026-03-08 - Priya Shah (SRE): Identified that the RBAC engine blocks on remote policy cache refresh during spikes; short-term mitigation is to serve stale policies for 60s with a metric flag.
2026-03-09 - Marco Ruiz (Security Eng): Proposed alert threshold changes to reduce pages from transient audit lag; opened PR #1527 to add delivery latency histogram to the sink.
2026-03-11 - Design Review (Leah/Marco/Ethan): Reviewed dashboard mockups; agreed to add a composite view for SSO flows showing 3 hops (proxy -> idp -> token service)
2026-03-12 - Leah Morrison: Draft runbooks added; requesting review from SRE and Security for escalation policy and mitigation steps.
postmortem_summary:
Root cause: combined capacity spike + a race in RBACv2's remote policy refresh caused >40% increase in auth evaluation latency for ~18 minutes; SAML requests experienced increased round-trips to the IDP when proxy connections were overloaded; audit pipeline experienced transient consumer lag due to unbalanced partitioning. Contributing factors: insufficient RBAC eval telemetry, alerting thresholds set on percent errors rather than latency-plus-queue-depth, and missing delivery timestamps for audit events.

Impact: Several customers reported login failures and delayed audit records ingestion. No evidence of data loss; all missing events were recovered within 6 hours after backfill.
action_items: Short-term: Enable serving stale RBAC policies for 60s during refresh hot-paths (owner: Marco Ruiz, ETA: 2026-03-14)
Telemetry: Instrument RBAC eval timing (p50/p95/p99) and export tag-by-policy to tracing (owner: Priya Shah, ETA: 2026-03-13)
SSO: Add end-to-end SSO synthetic checks across regions and pipeline to create SLO signals (owner: Leah Morrison, ETA: 2026-03-18)
Alerts: Replace the current auth error-rate page with combined latency+queue-depth alerts and add a 5-min suppressor for transient spikes (owner: SRE rotation, ETA: 2026-03-16)
Audit pipeline: Add delivery timestamp and histogram to primary sink, and adjust consumer partitioning to reduce hot partitions (owner: Data Eng, ETA: 2026-03-20)
Runbooks: Publish runbooks with step-by-step mitigation including "serve-stale-policies" toggle and audit-backfill play (owner: Security Eng, ETA: 2026-03-15)
audit_findings: No evidence of privileged escalation; RBAC policy integrity maintained
Audit sink lacked observable delivery timestamps making triage slower
Some SSO failures were amplified by aggressive retry policies between proxy and IDP
Access logs did not correlate request ID across components consistently
alert_changes: Introduce composite alert 'Auth: latency+queue' which fires when p99 latency > 200ms AND consumer queue depth > 1000
Lower noise by creating a multi-window alert that only pages if the condition persists for 10 minutes (otherwise create a ticket)
Add a 'Audit sink lag warning' at 30s and critical at 5 minutes with runbook link
Add synthetic SSO check failure alert scoped by region and IDP
